title: Inference hypernotes: KV eviction & streaming roughs
content:
Quick context: scribbling down ideas from recent reads + tiny experiments. Goal is a short checklist of micro-experiments I can run on dedicated infra and notes for a potential eval doc. Mostly rough, triage later into a proper PRD/benchmark.

Top-level question
- How much does aggressive KV eviction hurt long-tail coherence vs how much cost do we save in peak memory? Is there a sweet spot that depends on prompt distribution (chain-of-thought vs short instruction)?

Notes from papers & talks (very terse)
- Paper: "Prefix-aware KV compression (arXiv 2303.17580)" — idea: compress old KV strata with lightweight lossy quantization, then decompress when accessed. Tradeoff: decompression tail latency when cold access.
- Talk: SRE@NeurIPS 2028 keynote about graceful degradation — fallback to smaller context slice + rerank top-k completions when KV miss rate spikes.
- Blog: "Streaming transformers in production" — streaming tradeoffs: immediate partial tokens vs coherent higher-level state; prefer chunked autoregressive decoding with soft commit points.

Personal micro-experiments to run (priority order)
1) Eviction policy sweep (setup: small Llama-ish base on 2xA10G dev cluster)
   - Policies: LRU global, LRU per-seq, age-threshold (time-based), freq-weighted (LFU-ish), hybrid (age+freq)
   - Metric: per-token tail latency (95/99), end-to-end response coherence (BLEU-ish proxy: next-sentence perplexity), memory footprint (GB/GPU)
   - Quick plan: run with synthetic prompt mix: 60% short (~50 tokens), 30% med (200 tokens), 10% long (2-4k tokens). Baseline = no-eviction for 10k requests. Each sweep: 5k requests warmup + 5k measured.
   - Expected: age-based should preserve recent context for interactive apps; freq helps for reused retrievals (RAG)

2) Compressed-tier prototype
   - Idea: move KV buckets older than N tokens to compressed tier (4-bit/q4 variants) and hold meta indexes. Access penalty: decompress single KV chunk on miss.
   - Measure: additional latency on first access vs subsequent accesses; also throughput impact under concurrent demand.
   - Safety: have automatic fallback to full-resolution model when decompress fails or latency > SLO.

3) Streaming + partial KV commit experiment
   - Sketch: for long streaming responses, periodically checkpoint KV state to a small on-device cache and mark previous states as checkpointed (evict original). On backtracking or edit, rehydrate.
   - Metric: perceived streaming responsiveness (time-to-first-byte), frequency of rehydrate events in realistic dialogue traces.

Quick findings from tiny local runs (11/2028)
- LRU global vs per-seq: global LRU kept more cross-conversation reuse (helpful for demos) but occasionally thrashes when many concurrent long sessions; per-seq safer for privacy isolation and stable latencies.
- Age-threshold delta: eviction at 30s vs 120s changes GPU memory by ~1.2GB on small model with high-turn traffic. Coherence drop measured: ~3-5% on next-sentence scoring when threshold at 30s for long narratives.

Open questions / weird observations
- When using q4 compression for cached KV, some rare tokens (unicode emoji sequences) cause bigger reconstruction errors; need targeted tests on token distribution.
- Does batch size interact with eviction policy effectiveness? Hypothesis: larger batches homogenize accesses and reduce miss penalties.
- How to quantify "coherence degradation" beyond simple next-token perplexity? Need human evaluation or proxy metrics (contradiction detector, instruction-following checklist).

Notes-to-self: evaluation proxies to implement
- Chain-of-thought integrity check: insert synthetic multi-step reasoning tasks; count number of reasoning steps preserved after cold-rehydrate.
- Instruction fidelity metric: run a suite of 120 instruction prompts and compute instruction-error regression compared to baseline.
- Latency SLO simulator: synthetic spike generator to mimic 10x burst for 30s; measure model fallbacks and time to recovery.

Implementation hints (snippets)
- KV chunk ID scheme: <session-id>::<epoch-window-start>::<kv-shard-id>
- Maintain tiny bloom filter per-GPU to quickly test compressed-tier membership before attempting decompress (saves DMA cycles).
- Use asynchronous decompress worker pool with prioritized queue for tail-critical paths.

Next steps (this week)
- Triage resource allocation with infra: request 2xA10G for 72h for full sweep (CC: infra). Put ticket in JIRA-INF-9876.
- Prototype tiny compressor using existing q4 quant lib (Evan's fork). Try naive decompress-on-demand, measure p99.
- Draft short internal note summarizing initial findings and recommended policy defaults for Redwood Dedicated customers.

Loose brainstorming (low effort) — for later
- Hybrid networked KV: keep hot keys local, reference cold compressed keys via a remote mini-store (fast NVMe+RDMA). If remote seen > threshold, promote to local.
- Policy UI: in Console, expose "eviction aggressiveness" slider that maps to concrete thresholds (time, size, percent compressed).

References / reading queue
- arXiv:2303.17580 (prefix compression)
- blog: "Streaming transformers in production" (link above)
- internal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments/pull/12
- talk notes: SRE keynote NeurIPS 2028 (local notes)

Random TODOs / reminders
- Ask Maya about dataset of long-dialogue traces she mentioned (possible seed set for coherence tests)
- Check with growth/solutions whether users would accept occasional rehydrate latency in exchange for lower costs (product tradeoff)

End of scratchpad. Export later into a structured evaluation doc (csv + small runners).
